name: Euler’s fluid-motion equations
description: Continuum differential equations for ideal fluid motion.

impact.note: First field equations for fluid motion, used by one profession across countries; theoretical fluid dynamics grew from them.

date.basis: Year of the source-bounded episode, not necessarily invention.

evidence.supports: Dates publication to 1757, Mémoires volume 11, pp. 274–315.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated source-bounded episode in this record, not a claim of worldwide priority.

caveats: Euler’s earlier 1752 Latin paper had a restrictive vorticity assumption and appeared in print later; 1755 presentation days differ across historical sources. The equations represent idealized fluids, not all viscous fluid behavior.
